newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-BLACK VAULTS INTO ONE-STROKE LEAD IN LAS VEGAS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BLACK VAULTS INTO ONE-STROKE LEAD IN LAS VEGAS.

text.p: Relatively unknown Ronnie
Black jumped into a one-shot lead going into the final round
of the Las Vegas Invitational golf tournament with a
six-under-par 66 on Saturday.
The 38-year-old Black, who entered the tournament just
123rd on the PGA Tour's money list, knows he faces a daunting
challenge, but says he's up to winning the $297,000
first-place prize. But the big names are lurking close to him
on the leader board.
Davis Love III is alone in second at 22-under 265, while
Fred Couples and Dave Stockton Jr. are another shot back at
266. And at 267 is Fred Funk, the hottest player on Tour, and
Dan Pohl.
"Fred and Davis both are better players than I am," Black
said. "But you know what? I can beat them tomorrow. Tomorrow,
I can beat them. On this golf course, I can.
"The way I'm playing, the way I'm putting, on this golf
course, I can get it done. I'm not saying I'm going to. I'm
just saying I have potential and I'm playing well enough to do
it."
Black began the day three shots behind third-round leader
Rick Fehr, who ballooned to a 1-over 73 and is four shots off
the pace.
Black got moving early, starting his day by nearly holing
his approach. He hit a pitching wedge to within two inches of
the cup and tapped in for birdie.
He then two-putted for a birdie on the par-5 third hole
and sank putts of 20 feet and 18 feet for birdies on 4 and 6,
respectively, to make the turn at 4-under.
Love did nothing spectacular, but managed to stay out of
trouble most of the day and birdied two of the final four
holes to get within a shot of Black's lead.
Couples had a chance to be in the lead, but parred the
par-5 16th when he might have had a chance for eagle. He put
his approach shot into the lake guarding the green and had to
get up and down for par.
He wasn't pleased with his play on that hole.
"The one on 16 was ridiculous," Couples said. "The green is
as big as Las Vegas, and I just didn't hit it far enough to
get it past (trouble). I pushed it."
